rows.title: get_in and update_in must stop at a value that is not an array
body: Bug: get_in(["foo" => null], ["foo", "bar"]) and get_in(["key" => "value"], ["key", "x"], "default") fail instead of returning the default, because the walk keeps indexing into a null or scalar.

Outcome: get_in returns its default when the path goes through a value that is not an array; update_in throws InvalidArgumentException for the same path. Existing behaviour is unchanged. Fix src/get_in.php and add a test.

rows.title: parse-link-header cuts a URL that contains a semicolon
body: Bug: parsing '<https://imaginary.url.notreal/segment;foo=bar;baz/item?name=What,+me+worry>; rel="next";' loses the part of the URL after the first ';'.
Outcome: the URL is taken up to the closing '>' before the attributes are split on ';', so the url field is the whole URL. Existing behaviour is unchanged. Fix index.js and add a test.

rows.title: unzip-http extracts zip members outside the target directory
body: Bug (Zip Slip): member names come from the archive, so '../x', '/tmp/x' or 'sub/../../x' escape the target path in RemoteZipFile.extract() and in the CLI -f (full filepaths) branch.

Outcome: a member whose resolved path is outside the target directory raises an Exception whose message contains 'unsafe path' and writes nothing; members inside the target extract as before. Fix unzip_http.py and add a test.

rows.title: assoc_in must replace a nested value that is not an array
body: The test suite is red on this base: tests/GetInTest.php case testAssocIn #4 fails. assoc_in(["foo" => null], ["foo", "bar"], "new value") does not build the missing level when the value on the path is null or a scalar.
Outcome: assoc_in replaces a non-array value on the path with an array and sets the new value; the whole existing test file passes. Fix src/get_in.php; do not edit the existing tests.

rows.title: ConfigCommentParser drops a __proto__ key from its results
body: Bug (npm workspaces monorepo, package packages/plugin-kit): parseStringConfig and parseListConfig build their result as a plain object literal, so a '__proto__' item in the comment is lost instead of being kept as an own property.

Outcome: both methods return a map with a null prototype (Object.create(null)), so '__proto__' is an ordinary own key; the keys and values are otherwise unchanged. Fix packages/plugin-kit/src/config-comment-parser.js and add tests in packages/plugin-kit/tests/config-comment-parser.test.js.

rows.title: Ymir WordPress plugin builds WP-CLI commands with unescaped shell arguments
body: Bug (WordPress plugin): LambdaClient wraps the site URL, option values and image changes in hand-written single quotes, so a value containing a quote runs as shell.

Outcome: every value is passed as one POSIX-quoted shell argument (a single quote becomes '\'' and multibyte text is kept as is); a value with a null byte, and image changes that are not valid JSON, throw InvalidArgumentException before anything is invoked (the JSON message is: The given image "changes" must be valid JSON). Fix src/CloudProvider/Aws/LambdaClient.php and add tests in tests/Unit/CloudProvider/Aws/LambdaClientTest.php. The tests need a WordPress core checkout; the test command already sets WP_CORE_DIR to one.

rows.title: tailwind-merge misses the conflict when a class has an important modifier and a postfix modifier
body: Bug (frontend class-name component, package packages/tailwind-merge): twMerge('!text-lg/7 !text-sm') returns both classes although both set font-size as important; the same class without the leading '!' or with a trailing 'text-lg/7!' merges correctly.

Outcome: a leading important modifier does not shift the postfix modifier position, so '!text-lg/7 !text-sm' gives '!text-sm', '!text-lg/7 !text-lg/9' gives '!text-lg/9' and '!text-lg/7 !text-sm/6' gives '!text-sm/6'; existing behaviour is unchanged. Fix packages/tailwind-merge/src/lib/parse-class-name.ts and add tests in packages/tailwind-merge/tests/important-modifier.test.ts.
